text: On the chat_preference testbed, we evaluated a method that scores training examples by the alignment between weak labels and the strong model's embedding geometry, retains the top-scoring half, and fine-tunes on that subset. The run yielded a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.75. Several caveats materially limit what can be drawn from this. The configuration reports no num_seeds, so the number of replicates behind the 0.75 figure is unknown and no variance or standard error is available; we therefore cannot assess run-to-run spread or attach any uncertainty interval to the point estimate. No baseline PGR is provided either, so the 0.75 cannot be characterized as an improvement over an unfiltered or randomly filtered fine-tuning control, nor over any other selection strategy. The result is best read as a single reported measurement on one testbed, pending repeated seeds and a matched baseline before any comparative or confidence claim is made.
